text:
ashok: noticed a spike last night where CA spun up a bunch of 4-GPU nodes but most pods only need 1 GPU. tons of wasted capacity.
maria: ugh yeah saw that in cost dashboard. fragmentation again. which expander are we using?
ashok: currently `--expander=most-pods` for nodepool-multi-gpu. goal was to maximize pod count per scale-up. apparently backfired for bursty 1-GPU workloads.
sanjay: can we try `least-waste`? CA docs say it prefers nodes that minimize leftover resources. might be better when requests are single-gpu.
maria: least-waste helped in one project but caused noisy churn because it adds many small nodes. with spot mixing we got more preemptions.
cami: what about a burst-splitting approach: keep 4-GPU nodepools for steady throughput, but have a small on-demand 1-GPU burst pool for spikes. CA should target the 1-GPU pool first for new pods.
ashok: that matches what I was thinking. we can use nodeSelector/taints to steer ephemeral GPU jobs into burst pool. plus set CA expander to `most-pods` in burst pool and `least-waste` in the multi-gpu pool? CA expander is global tho...
maria: true CA flag is cluster-wide. but we can use separate nodegroups and labels and rely on pod scheduling + provisioning priorities (podPriorityClass + nodeAffinity) so CA picks the right group. also k8s supports scale-down delay overrides per node group in some cloud providers.
sanjay: example resource request -> set podPriority to higher for latency-critical jobs so they prefer smaller on-demand nodes. cheaper batch jobs get lower priority and pack into the 4-GPU nodes.
cami: here's a candidate CA flags snippet for testing in staging:
```
--balance-similar-node-groups
--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.25
--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m
--max-total-unready-percentage=10
--ok-total-unready-count=3
```
maria: add `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false` so CA considers nodes with daemonsets for scale-down budgeting, we currently leak nodes that look occupied only by system pods.
ashok: good call. also add limits: `--max-gpus-total=800` so staging doesn't blow into prod quota mistakes.
sanjay: how do we detect fragmentation? we should add a panel: GPU idle minutes per node + fraction of nodes <50% GPU utilization. sample query: `sum by(node)(gpu_utilization_seconds_total) / (node_gpu_count * 60)` — rough idea.
maria: we already emit `kube_pod_container_resource_requests_gpu` in prometheus. query: `sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests_gpu) by (node)` vs `node_gpu_capacity` will show gaps.
cami: plan for rollout: 1) create 1-GPU on-demand burst nodepool with taint `gpu-burst=true:NoSchedule` 2) update CI job specs to tolerate that taint for low-latency jobs 3) adjust CA flags in staging and run 24h canary 4) monitor fragmentation and preemptions
ashok: action items: I will open a kustomize PR to add new nodepool and CA flags toggle (staging-only).
maria: I can add dash panels and an alert: `GPU_fragmentation_ratio > 0.4 for 30m` -> slack notify #eng-infra.
sanjay: I'll draft podPriority mappings for latency vs batch and a migration plan for batch jobs.
cami: tagging: @ops-bot please create a ticket in JIRA with these steps and link the kustomize PR once opened.
ops-bot: created ticket INFRA-3127 "burst 1-GPU pool + CA tuning canary" and assigned to @ashok. due 2026-06-05. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: canary deployment triggered for staging/autoscaler-config v2 at 1769003602
maria: thanks — let's let the canary run overnight and regroup tomorrow morning. short follow-ups only in this thread. :+1:
